items.extract: Release: llm-gemini 0.37 Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen today - the lowest cost member of the Gemini 4 family. It's actually not too far off the price of its much bigger siblings, Carbon and Argon. I'm finding Gemini 4's pricing really confusing. Here's the pricing scheme: Model Dates Input ($/M) Cached input Output Gemini 4 Carbon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Argon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Hydrogen $1.50 $0.075 $7.50 Carbon and Argon are the same price , and both are scheduled to double in price on December 1st.

clusters.headline: llm 0.37.2

items.title: llm 0.37.2
items.extract: Release: llm 0.37.2 Fixes a security issue reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w . LLM has a mechanism called extra-openai-models.yaml - now managed by the new-in-0.37 llm openai endpoint add command - for using LLM with OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. Daniel reported two ways this could accidentally send your configured OpenAI API key to one of those providers: if the key named by api_key_name had never been stored, or if a responses: true model was run with -o chat_completions 1 . Tags: projects , security , llm , releases

clusters.summary: The llm 0.37.2 release fixes two security vulnerabilities reported by Daniel de Araujo under identifiers GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w. These flaws involved the extra-openai-models.yaml mechanism—which is used alongside the llm openai endpoint add command introduced in version 0.37 for OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. The reported issues could cause a configured OpenAI API key to be accidentally sent to an external provider if the key specified by api_key_name lacked stored data or if a responses: true model executed with the -o chat_completions 1 flag.

clusters.headline: AI Text Watermarking May Not Be Able to Meet the E.U.’s New Rules

items.title: AI Text Watermarking May Not Be Able to Meet the E.U.’s New Rules
items.extract: The European Union now requires AI-generated text to be watermarked so that it can be identified as such. But tests on OpenAI’s new textGrain watermark, released in October and developed to comply with the new E.U. law , show that these watermarks often do not survive additional editing of the text or when it’s under 150 words. With no clear legal benchmark for how well watermarks should work, it’s uncertain whether textGrain will meet Europe’s transparency rules, which could cost the company significantly and make it difficult to detect AI-generated text as models grow more sophisticated.

clusters.summary: OpenAI's textGrain watermark, released in October to comply with new European Union rules requiring AI-generated text to be watermarked, often fails when text is edited or falls under 150 words. Because the E.U. lacks a clear legal benchmark for watermark effectiveness, it remains uncertain if textGrain will satisfy these transparency regulations. This uncertainty could lead to significant financial costs for OpenAI and hinder the detection of advanced AI text.

clusters.headline: How a Kenyan Startup Is Rethinking AI for Small Businesses

items.title: How a Kenyan Startup Is Rethinking AI for Small Businesses
items.extract: The first time Mutembei Kariuki thought about how AI models could work in Kenya, his home country, was in 2019. He was attending a conference at the University of Tokyo on the future of AI, and kept hearing about how this technology was going to transform the world. “But nobody mentioned Africa at all,” he says. Even then—before AI giants like OpenAI and Anthropic had launched their chatbots to the public—Kariuki could see significant obstacles to AI adoption in Africa. Internet access was slow and unequal, computing resources for training models were scarce, and there was little high-quality, structured training data.

clusters.summary: In 2019, Kenyan founder Mutembei Kariuki began rethinking artificial intelligence for small businesses after attending a University of Tokyo conference on the future of AI where Africa was entirely unmentioned. Even prior to the public launches of chatbots from major AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, Kariuki identified major barriers to artificial intelligence adoption across Africa. These hurdles included slow and uneven internet connectivity, a scarcity of computing resources required for training models, and a lack of high-quality, structured training data.

clusters.headline: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?

items.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
items.extract: Applying machine learning systems to new domains introduces bottlenecks in both labeled data acquisition and manual pipeline engineering. While recent MLE agents show promise in automating pipeline design, they have been studied almost exclusively in fully supervised settings, leaving them untested in realistic regimes where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled data is abundant. In this work, we introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL), framing SSL as a program search problem and studying how agents navigate this space under limited supervision.

clusters.summary: Researchers have introduced Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning, or AgentSSL, a novel approach that frames semi-supervised learning as a program search problem to investigate whether machine learning engineering agents can utilize unlabeled data. Current machine learning systems face hurdles in acquiring labeled data and handling manual pipeline engineering when applied to new domains. Although recent machine learning engineering agents demonstrate potential in automating pipeline design, prior research has focused almost exclusively on fully supervised settings, leaving these agents untested in realistic environments where labeled data is scarce and unlabeled data is plentiful. The new AgentSSL framework explores how these agents operate within this search space when supervision is restricted.

items.extract: Nebius plans to fund its $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion through customer prepayments and loans, even as delays at a Microsoft data center raise questions about its financing model.

clusters.summary: Nebius intends to finance its $40 billion artificial intelligence infrastructure growth via customer prepayments and loans, despite questions regarding its funding model stemming from delays at a Microsoft data center. The company is putting its neocloud playbook to the test through this planned spending.

clusters.headline: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom

items.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
items.extract: Fully automated ransomware hasn’t arrived—yet. But seemingly unsophisticated attackers are using AI tools to wreak havoc.

clusters.summary: Unskilled threat actors are leveraging artificial intelligence tools to cause widespread disruption, though fully automated ransomware has not yet emerged. The situation marks a new boom in ransomware fueled by AI technology.

clusters.headline: How AI Is Helping Care Teams Get Patients the Right Care, Sooner

items.title: How AI Is Helping Care Teams Get Patients the Right Care, Sooner
items.extract: From pediatric research to smart hospitals, AI is helping care teams spend less time on routine tasks and more time with patients. Health systems and startups are putting it to work across healthcare, from matching patients to clinical trials to supporting radiologists, hospital teams and patients at home. Clinicians stay at the center, reviewing AI

clusters.summary: Artificial intelligence is assisting medical professionals in streamlining routine duties so they can dedicate additional time to patients. Healthcare organizations and startups are deploying this technology across various medical sectors, including aiding radiologists, supporting hospital teams, assisting patients at home, and connecting individuals with clinical trials, ranging from smart hospitals to pediatric research. Throughout these applications, physicians remain central by reviewing the technology's output.

clusters.headline: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas, part 1

items.title: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas, part 1
items.extract: GS Caltex connects Amazon SageMaker Canvas to Amazon SageMaker Pipelines so process engineers' no-code models run in production. This post shows how ML engineers reuse validated preprocessing flows and models, cutting deployment from about a week to a few hours and running batch inference every 30 minutes.

clusters.summary: GS Caltex has integrated Amazon SageMaker Canvas with Amazon SageMaker Pipelines to deploy no-code models built by process engineers into production. Through this integration, machine learning engineers are able to reuse validated preprocessing flows and models. This workflow reduces the deployment timeline from approximately a week down to just a few hours. Additionally, the system executes batch inference every 30 minutes.

clusters.headline: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard

items.title: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard
items.extract: Coding agents work in tasks, and the number that matters is cost per solved task, not price per token. In this post, you use the AWS CDK to deploy LiteLLM with the NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing plugin on Amazon Bedrock, then measure cost per solved task for a routed model group against single-model baselines.

clusters.summary: Amazon Bedrock now allows developers to route coding agent requests to the appropriate model using the NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing plugin. A new guide demonstrates how to deploy LiteLLM with this plugin on Amazon Bedrock using the AWS CDK. Practitioners can then measure the cost per solved task for a routed model group, comparing it against single-model baselines.

clusters.headline: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime

items.title: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
items.extract: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 snapshots your initialized environment and restores it for each new session, so session start no longer grows with image size. This post explains how V2 starts a session, how to measure session start time, and four patterns to keep work off the first request.

clusters.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 introduces snapshotting of initialized environments to restore them for each new session, preventing session start times from growing with image size. A recent post details the V2 session-start process, methods for measuring startup duration, and four distinct architectural patterns designed to offload work from the initial request.

clusters.headline: OpenFold3 on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: Predict biomolecular structures

items.title: OpenFold3 on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: Predict biomolecular structures
items.extract: Deploy OpenFold3-preview from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to predict 3D structures of proteins, DNA, RNA, and ligand complexes in your own AWS account. The post covers asynchronous inference, multi-GPU parallelism, bringing your own MSAs for accuracy and privacy, and scaling to zero to reduce cost.

clusters.summary: OpenFold3-preview is now available for deployment on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to forecast the 3D structures of ligand complexes, RNA, DNA, and proteins within a personal AWS account. The release highlights support for multi-GPU parallelism, asynchronous inference, bringing personal multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) for enhanced privacy and accuracy, and scaling to zero to minimize expenses.

clusters.headline: Cost-optimizing AssemblyAI speech-to-text inference on AWS with Amazon EC2 Spot

items.title: Cost-optimizing AssemblyAI speech-to-text inference on AWS with Amazon EC2 Spot
items.extract: Learn how AssemblyAI runs cost-optimized speech-to-text inference at scale on AWS, using Amazon ECS, Amazon EC2 Spot GPU instances, and an Amazon SQS-based retry architecture to achieve 70% cost savings while maintaining SLA commitments across European Regions.

clusters.summary: AssemblyAI has achieved 70% cost savings on AWS by running speech-to-text inference at scale using Amazon ECS, Amazon EC2 Spot GPU instances, and an Amazon SQS-based retry architecture. This cost-optimizing approach allows the company to maintain its service level agreement commitments across European Regions.

clusters.headline: Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock

items.title: Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock
items.extract: Amazon Bedrock provides built-in, zero-instrumentation cost attribution that traces every inference call back to the IAM principal that made it. This post shows how to attribute per-user Bedrock costs for AI developer and productivity tools using IAM Identity Center, session tags, and CUR 2.0, and how to enforce per-user usage limits.

clusters.summary: Amazon Bedrock now features native, zero-instrumentation cost attribution that maps every inference call directly to the IAM principal responsible. An official guide details methods for tracking individual user expenses related to AI developer and productivity tools by leveraging IAM Identity Center, session tags, and CUR 2.0. Additionally, the documentation outlines procedures for setting and enforcing per-user usage caps.

clusters.headline: Build a model improvement flywheel with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture

items.title: Build a model improvement flywheel with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture
items.extract: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture records live inference inputs and outputs to Amazon S3. This post walks through one end-to-end example: capturing a support router's production traffic, surfacing a new-product blind spot with Amazon Athena, fine-tuning on the captured data with the HyperPod training operator, and measuring the before-and-after lift.

clusters.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture has been introduced to record live inference inputs and outputs directly to Amazon S3. A published walkthrough demonstrates this capability using an end-to-end example that captures production traffic from a support router. The process involves identifying a new-product blind spot with Amazon Athena, fine-tuning the model on the captured data via the HyperPod training operator, and subsequently measuring the performance lift before and after the update.

clusters.headline: How Microcredentials Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

items.title: How Microcredentials Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI
items.extract: Engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics , governance , and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges. “AI ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

clusters.summary: Microcredentials help engineering teams address compliance issues as they integrate artificial intelligence. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry's toughest challenges as teams move at breakneck speed. AI ethics refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows, while governance is the set of rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and data interaction. Auditing involves assessing and validating systems to ensure they remain safe, fair, transparent, and legally compliant.

items.extract: Host Sowbhagya Suresh shares some of the latest news and cutting-edge research from across Microsoft—from understanding the challenges facing coding agents to uncovering how people use AI at work and improving extended-range weather forecasting.
